subject.title: Telegram bot cannot fetch media/images - MediaFetchError DNS issue

question: Should Telegram media downloads trust env-proxy target DNS after Telegram hostname-policy checks, or should env-proxy/no-DNS users remain on the current strict local-DNS behavior?
rationale: The observable bug is source-reproducible, but the fix changes how attacker-influenced Telegram file URLs interact with SSRF guard, proxy DNS, private-network policy, and redirects.

options.title: Sponsor narrow env-proxy media fix
options.body: Allow Telegram env-proxy media downloads to delegate target DNS to the proxy only after hostname allowlist, private-network, redirect, and token-redaction checks, with focused tests and live proof.

options.title: Keep strict local-DNS behavior
options.body: Document that Telegram media downloads require local DNS or explicit proxy configuration, accepting that env-proxy/no-DNS installs continue to fail media downloads.

options.title: Defer to broader egress refactor
options.body: Leave this issue open until a shared outbound-network policy redesign owns env-proxy DNS trust across media and provider fetches.

recommendation.title: Sponsor narrow env-proxy media fix
recommendation.body: Allow Telegram env-proxy media downloads to delegate target DNS to the proxy only after hostname allowlist, private-network, redirect, and token-redaction checks, with focused tests and live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Most recent concrete owner of the same Telegram media and guarded-fetch proxy DNS seam.
